name: branch_create
description: Create a branch in a GitHub repository, pointing at a branch, tag or commit. Use it to start work off the default branch or off another branch. Fails if the name is taken.

branch.description: Name of the new branch, e.g. 'feat/login'.

from.description: Branch, tag or commit sha to start from. Default: the repository's default branch.

name: branch_delete
description: Delete a branch from a GitHub repository. Destructive: commits only that branch holds become unreachable, so confirm with the owner first. The default branch cannot be deleted.

branch.description: Name of the branch to delete.

name: branch_list
description: List the branches of a GitHub repository, with the sha at each tip and whether it is protected. Paged. Use it to see what branches exist before creating, merging or deleting one.

protected.description: true lists only protected branches, false only unprotected ones. Omit for all.

name: branch_merge
description: Merge a branch (or commit) into another branch of a GitHub repository directly, with no pull request. Destructive: it moves the base branch, so confirm with the owner first. Use pr_merge when a pull request exists.

base.description: Branch that receives the merge, e.g. 'main'.

head.description: Branch or commit sha to merge into the base.

message.description: Commit message for the merge commit. Default: GitHub's.

name: branch_read
description: Read one branch of a GitHub repository: the commit at its tip, that commit's message and date, and whether the branch is protected. Use it to find a branch's current sha.

name: commit_compare
description: Compare two branches, tags or commits of a GitHub repository: how far ahead or behind the head is of the base, the most recent 50 commits between them, and the changed files with line counts. Use it to see what a branch would bring in before merging.

base.description: The ref to compare from, e.g. 'main'.

name: commit_list
description: List commits of a GitHub repository, newest first, from a branch, tag or sha, optionally only those touching a path, by an author, or within a date range. Paged. Use commit_read for one commit in full.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit sha to list back from. Default: the default branch.

path.description: Only commits that touched this file or directory.

author.description: Only commits by this GitHub login or email.

since.description: Only commits after this ISO 8601 date, e.g. 2026-10-01.

until.description: Only commits before this ISO 8601 date.

name: commit_read
description: Read one commit of a GitHub repository: its message, author, date, parents, the files it changed with their line counts, and optionally its diff (cut at 20,000 characters). Use it to see what a commit did. Defaults to the tip of the default branch.

ref.description: Commit sha, branch or tag. Default: the default branch's tip.

diff.description: true also returns the commit's diff. Default false.

name: directory_list
description: List the files and folders in one directory of a GitHub repository, on the default branch or at a branch, tag or commit. Not recursive. Omit the path for the repository root. Use it to find a path before file_read.

path.description: Directory inside the repository, e.g. 'src/tools'. Omit for the root.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit sha. Default: the default branch.

name: file_create
description: Create a new file in a GitHub repository, as one commit on a branch (default: the default branch). Fails if the file already exists; use file_update to change it. Content up to 1 MB.

path.description: Path of the new file, e.g. 'docs/notes.md'. Missing folders are created.

content.description: The file's full content. An empty string creates an empty file.

branch.description: Branch to commit to. Default: the default branch.

name: file_delete
description: Delete one file from a GitHub repository, as one commit on a branch (default: the default branch). Destructive: the file stays in history but leaves the branch, so confirm with the owner first. Reads the file's current sha first unless one is passed.

path.description: Path of the file to delete.

branch.description: Branch to commit to. Default: the default branch.

sha.description: Blob sha of the version being deleted (from file_read).

name: file_read
description: Read one text file from a GitHub repository, on the default branch or at a branch, tag or commit. Returns its content, size and blob sha. Cut at 25,000 characters; binary files and files over 1 MB are refused. Use directory_list to find a path first.

path.description: Path of the file inside the repository, e.g. 'src/index.js'.

ref.description: Branch, tag or commit sha. Default: the default branch.

name: file_update
description: Replace the content of an existing file in a GitHub repository, as one commit on a branch (default: the default branch). Reads the file's current sha first unless one is passed. Use file_create for a new file.

content.description: The file's new full content - not a patch.

branch.description: Branch to commit to. Default: the default branch.

sha.description: Blob sha of the version being replaced (from file_read). Pass it to fail if the file changed since.

name: issue_assign
description: Add, remove or replace the assignees of an issue (or pull request) in a GitHub repository. GitHub ignores people who cannot be assigned, such as non-collaborators; the result lists any it did not apply.

assignees.description: GitHub logins. At most 10 when adding.

action.description: add (default) keeps the current assignees and adds these; remove takes these off; set replaces all.

name: issue_close
description: Close an issue of a GitHub repository, as completed, not planned or a duplicate, optionally leaving a comment first. It only closes: there is no tool to reopen. Use pr_close for a pull request.

comment.description: A comment to post before closing, e.g. why.

name: issue_comment
description: Add a comment to an issue of a GitHub repository. Works on a pull request's number too, as a conversation comment. Visible to everyone who can see the issue.

name: issue_label
description: Add, remove or replace the labels on an issue (or pull request) in a GitHub repository. The result lists the labels now on the issue and any requested label that is not as asked.

action.description: add (default) keeps the current labels and adds these; remove takes these off; set replaces all.

name: issue_lock
description: Lock an issue or pull request in a GitHub repository so only collaborators can comment, with an optional reason, or unlock it. Needs push access.

reason.description: Why it is locked: off-topic, too heated, resolved or spam. Only when locking.

name: issue_open
description: Open a new issue in a GitHub repository, with optional body, labels, assignees and milestone. GitHub ignores labels, assignees and milestone from a token without push access; the result lists what was actually applied.

labels.description: Label names to apply. They must already exist.

name: issue_read
description: Read one issue of a GitHub repository: title, state, author, labels, assignees, milestone and body, and with `comments: true` its first 30 comments. Also works on a pull request's number, and says when it is one; use pr_read for its branches and diff.

comments.description: true also returns the first 30 comments. Default false.

name: pr_approve
description: Approve a pull request in a GitHub repository as the token's user, with an optional message. A person cannot approve their own pull request. Each call records another approval review.

body.description: A message to go with the approval.

sha.description: The head commit being approved; the approval fails if the branch has moved on. Default: the latest.

name: pr_close
description: Close a pull request in a GitHub repository without merging it, optionally leaving a comment first. Its branch is kept. There is no tool to reopen it.

comment.description: A comment to post before closing, e.g. why.

name: pr_comment
description: Add a comment to a pull request's conversation in a GitHub repository. A conversation comment only: it is not attached to a line of the diff and is not a review. Visible to everyone who can see the pull request.

name: pr_merge
description: Merge a pull request in a GitHub repository, by merge commit, squash or rebase. Destructive: it moves the base branch, so confirm with the owner first. Pass `sha` to merge only if the branch is still at the commit that was reviewed.

method.description: merge (default), squash or rebase. The repository may disable some.

title.description: Title for the merge or squash commit. Default: GitHub's.

message.description: Body for the merge or squash commit. Default: GitHub's.

sha.description: The head commit the merge must match; a moved branch is refused (409).

name: pr_open
description: Open a pull request in a GitHub repository from a branch into a base branch (default: the default branch), optionally as a draft. For a branch in a fork, give the head as 'owner:branch'. Fails if there are no commits between them or one is already open.

head.description: Branch with the changes, e.g. 'feat/login', or 'owner:branch' for a fork.

base.description: Branch to merge into. Default: the repository's default branch.

draft.description: true opens it as a draft. Default false.

name: pr_read
description: Read one pull request of a GitHub repository: state, draft, merged, whether it can be merged, branches, size, labels, requested reviewers and description, and with `files: true` the first 100 changed files. Use issue_read with `comments: true` for the discussion.

files.description: true also lists the changed files, without their diffs. Default false.

name: pr_review_request
description: Request a review of a pull request in a GitHub repository from people, teams, or both. Reviewers must be collaborators and cannot be the pull request's author. Give at least one.

name: release_create
description: Create a release for a tag in a GitHub repository, creating the tag from a branch or commit if it does not exist. Can be a draft or prerelease, and can have GitHub write the notes. This is also how a tag is created.

tag.description: Tag for the release, e.g. 'v1.2.0'. Created if it does not exist.

target.description: Branch or commit sha to create the tag from. Default: the default branch. Ignored if the tag exists.

draft.description: true creates an unpublished draft. Default false.

prerelease.description: true marks it as a prerelease. Default false.

generate_notes.description: true has GitHub write the notes from merged pull requests, added to any body given.

name: release_delete
description: Delete a release of a GitHub repository, by tag or by id. Destructive: its notes and assets are lost, so confirm with the owner first. The tag is kept; use tag_delete to remove that too. Finds drafts by tag as well.

tag.description: Tag of the release to delete. Give this or release_id.

release_id.description: Id of the release (from release_list). Give this or tag.

name: release_list
description: List the releases of a GitHub repository, newest first, including drafts when the token has push access. Paged. Use release_read for one release's notes and assets.

name: release_read
description: Read one release of a GitHub repository: title, notes, whether it is a draft or prerelease, and its assets. Give a tag, or omit it for the latest published release. Finds drafts by tag too.

tag.description: Tag of the release. Omit for the latest published, non-prerelease one.

name: repo_create
description: Create a new, empty repository on GitHub and return its URLs. Use this when the owner asks to start a new GitHub repository, in their own account or in an organization. Private unless told otherwise. It only creates: it does not clone, push to, change or delete anything. The token is read from the GITHUB_API_KEY environment variable of the server, never from an argument.

name.description: Repository name: letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', at most 100 characters. Example: 'my-new-repo'.

org.description: Organization to create it in. Omit to create it in the personal account that owns the token. Example: 'LXAgents-MCP'.

description.description: One-line description shown on the repository.

private.description: Default true. Pass false only when the owner asked for a public repository.

auto_init.description: Default true: create an initial commit with a README, so the repository can be cloned straight away. Pass false for a truly empty repository.

name: repo_delete
description: Permanently delete a GitHub repository, with its issues, pull requests and wiki. Destructive and not undoable from here: confirm with the owner first. `confirm` must repeat the repository's full name. Needs delete rights on the token and admin on the repository.

confirm.description: The repository's full name again, 'owner/name'. Anything else deletes nothing.

name: repo_fork
description: Fork a GitHub repository into the token owner's account or an organization. GitHub copies it in the background, so the fork may take a moment to be readable. Use it to work on a repository the owner cannot push to.

organization.description: Organization to fork into. Omit to fork into the token owner's account.

name.description: Name for the fork. Omit to keep the source's name.

default_branch_only.description: true copies only the default branch. Default false.

name: repo_read
description: Read one GitHub repository: description, visibility, default branch, star, fork and issue counts, language, license, topics and parent. Use it to learn about a repository before acting on it.

name: repo_search
description: Search GitHub repositories with GitHub's search syntax, such as 'org:LXAgents-MCP mcp in:name' or 'topic:mcp language:javascript'. Use it to find a repository when the owner is not known. GitHub serves at most the first 1000 matches and limits search to 30 requests a minute.

query.description: Keywords and qualifiers, e.g. 'mcp in:name org:LXAgents-MCP' or 'user:octocat archived:false'.

sort.description: stars, forks, help-wanted-issues or updated. Default: best match.

order.description: asc or desc (default). Only applies when sort is given.

name: repo_update
description: Change a GitHub repository's settings: rename it, set its description or homepage, make it private or public, change the default branch, archive or unarchive it, or switch issues on or off. Pass only what should change; at least one setting is required.

name.description: New repository name. Renaming redirects the old name.

description.description: New description. Pass an empty string to clear it.

homepage.description: New homepage URL. Pass an empty string to clear it.

private.description: true makes the repository private, false makes it public.

default_branch.description: Branch to make the default. It must already exist.

archived.description: true archives the repository (read-only), false unarchives it.

has_issues.description: Whether the Issues tab is enabled.

name: tag_check
description: Check whether a tag exists in a GitHub repository, and if it does, what it points at and whether it is annotated. A missing tag is an answer, not an error. Use it before creating a release, or to avoid reusing a tag name.

name: tag_delete
description: Delete a tag from a GitHub repository. Destructive: anything that pins the tag, such as a release, loses its anchor, so confirm with the owner first. Deleting a release does not delete its tag, and this does not delete the release.

tag.description: Name of the tag to delete.

name: tag_get_all
description: List the tags of a GitHub repository with the commit each points at. Paged, in the order GitHub returns them (newest first for version-like names). Use it to see what has been tagged or released.

name: tag_get
description: Read one tag of a GitHub repository: the commit it points at and, for an annotated tag, its message, tagger and date. Use it to find the commit behind a version tag. tag_check only says whether a tag exists.

name: workflow_list
description: List the GitHub Actions workflows of a repository with their id, name, file path and state. Paged. Use it to find the workflow to run or to follow; the id or the file name, such as 'ci.yml', identifies it.

name: workflow_logs
description: Read the logs of the jobs of a GitHub Actions workflow run. By default only the failed jobs, up to 5, each cut to its last lines, where a failure is explained; job_id reads one job and only_failed false reads every job. At most 20,000 characters in all. Find run and job ids with workflow_status.

job_id.description: Read just this job of the run. Default: the failed jobs.

only_failed.description: false reads every job of the run, not only the failed ones. Default true. Ignored with job_id.

name: workflow_run
description: Start a GitHub Actions workflow run on a branch or tag (default: the default branch), with optional inputs. It runs whatever the workflow does, which may deploy or publish. The workflow needs an 'on: workflow_dispatch' trigger and its file must be on the default branch. Returns the run id when GitHub gives it; follow the run with workflow_status.

workflow.description: Workflow id or file name, e.g. 'ci.yml'. See workflow_list.

ref.description: Branch or tag to run it on. Default: the repository's default branch.

inputs.description: The workflow's inputs by name, up to 25. Values are sent as text.

name: workflow_status
description: Read a GitHub Actions workflow run: its status and conclusion, branch, commit, and each job's result with the step that failed. Give a run_id, or a workflow (optionally on a branch) to read its latest run. After workflow_run, ask again until the status is 'completed'.

run_id.description: Run id, from workflow_run or an earlier workflow_status.

workflow.description: Workflow id or file name, e.g. 'ci.yml'; reads its most recent run.

branch.description: With `workflow`: only runs on this branch.
